mentions.name: Chessnawk
mentions.description: A set of auto-grading programming tasks for middle school students, featuring Robot, Turtle, and HTML/CSS pixel-diff exercises that gradually introduce programming concepts. Currently supports JavaScript with Python being added, includes a simplified clone of Replicube, and plans to incorporate ideas from Human Resource Machine and Turing Complete. Intended for the community of secondary school CS teachers.
mentions.problem: Existing tools lack depth and usability in the classroom for ordinary 12-year-old kids learning programming.
mentions.audience: Nothing comes close in terms of depth and usability in the classroom for ordinary 12-year-old kids learning programming.

mentions.name: chessnawk
mentions.description: This app is an online collection of introductory programming exercises for middle school computer science. It includes turtle-graphics exercises using a small custom DSL (e.g., 4[100 r90] draws a square), Blockly-based robot exercises, and a 2D replica of Replicube for teaching conditions in JavaScript. New exercises are added as needed for the author's classroom, signups are coming soon, and the platform will be free forever, monetized later via banner ads.
mentions.audience: middle school teachers of Computer Science
mentions.source_excerpt: Currently I develop an online collection of exercises for intro to programming.
